24:16.ar: وَلَوۡلَآ إِذۡ سَمِعۡتُمُوهُ قُلۡتُم مَّا يَكُونُ لَنَآ أَن نَّتَكَلَّمَ بِهَٰذَا سُبۡحَٰنَكَ هَٰذَا بُهۡتَٰنٌ عَظِيمࣱ‏
24:16.en: Wherefor, when ye heard it, said ye not: It is not for us to speak of this. Glory be to Thee (O Allah)! This is awful calumny

24:27.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَدۡخُلُواْ بُيُوتًا غَيۡرَ بُيُوتِكُمۡ حَتَّىٰ تَسۡتَأۡنِسُواْ وَتُسَلِّمُواْ عَلَىٰٓ أَهۡلِهَاۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَذَكَّرُونَ
24:27.en: O ye who believe! Enter not houses other than your own without first announcing your presence and invoking peace upon the folk thereof. That is better for you, that ye may be heedful

24:28.ar: فَإِن لَّمۡ تَجِدُواْ فِيهَآ أَحَدࣰ ا فَلَا تَدۡخُلُوهَا حَتَّىٰ يُؤۡذَنَ لَكُمۡۖ وَإِن قِيلَ لَكُمُ ٱرۡجِعُواْ فَٱرۡجِعُواْۖ هُوَ أَزۡكَىٰ لَكُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ عَلِيمࣱ‏
24:28.en: And if ye find no-one therein, still enter not until permission hath been given. And if it be said unto you: Go away again, then go away, for it is purer for you. Allah knoweth what ye do

24:30.ar: قُل لِّلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ يَغُضُّواْ مِنۡ أَبۡصَٰرِهِمۡ وَيَحۡفَظُواْ فُرُوجَهُمۡۚ ذَٰلِكَ أَزۡكَىٰ لَهُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ خَبِيرُۢ بِمَا يَصۡنَعُونَ
24:30.en: Tell the believing men to lower their gaze and be modest. That is purer for them. Lo! Allah is aware of what they do

24:31.ar: وَقُل لِّلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِ يَغۡضُضۡنَ مِنۡ أَبۡصَٰرِهِنَّ وَيَحۡفَظۡنَ فُرُوجَهُنَّ وَلَا يُبۡدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إِلَّا مَا ظَهَرَ مِنۡهَاۖ وَلۡيَضۡرِبۡنَ بِخُمُرِهِنَّ عَلَىٰ جُيُوبِهِنَّۖ وَلَا يُبۡدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إِلَّا لِبُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوۡ ءَابَآئِهِنَّ أَوۡ ءَابَآءِ بُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوۡ أَبۡنَآئِهِنَّ أَوۡ أَبۡنَآءِ بُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوۡ إِخۡوَٰنِهِنَّ أَوۡ بَنِيٓ إِخۡوَٰنِهِنَّ أَوۡ بَنِيٓ أَخَوَٰتِهِنَّ أَوۡ نِسَآئِهِنَّ أَوۡ مَا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُهُنَّ أَوِ ٱلتَّٰبِعِينَ غَيۡرِ أُوْلِي ٱلۡإِرۡبَةِ مِنَ ٱلرِّجَالِ أَوِ ٱلطِّفۡلِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَمۡ يَظۡهَرُواْ عَلَىٰ عَوۡرَٰتِ ٱلنِّسَآءِۖ وَلَا يَضۡرِبۡنَ بِأَرۡجُلِهِنَّ لِيُعۡلَمَ مَا يُخۡفِينَ مِن زِينَتِهِنَّۚ وَتُوبُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ جَمِيعًا أَيُّهَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُفۡلِحُونَ
24:31.en: And tell the believing women to lower their gaze and be modest, and to display of their adornment only that which is apparent, and to draw their veils over their bosoms, and not to reveal their adornment save to their own husbands or fathers or husbands' fathers, or their sons or their husbands' sons, or their brothers or their brothers' sons or sisters' sons, or their women, or their slaves, or male attendants who lack vigour, or children who know naught of women's nakedness. And let them not stamp their feet so as to reveal what they hide of their adornment. And turn unto Allah together, O believers, in order that ye may succeed

24:32.ar: وَأَنكِحُواْ ٱلۡأَيَٰمَىٰ مِنكُمۡ وَٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ مِنۡ عِبَادِكُمۡ وَإِمَآئِكُمۡۚ إِن يَكُونُواْ فُقَرَآءَ يُغۡنِهِمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضۡلِهِۦۗ وَٱللَّهُ وَٰسِعٌ عَلِيمࣱ‏
24:32.en: And marry such of you as are solitary and the pious of your slaves and maid-servants. If they be poor, Allah will enrich them of His bounty. Allah is of ample means, Aware

24:33.ar: وَلۡيَسۡتَعۡفِفِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَجِدُونَ نِكَاحًا حَتَّىٰ يُغۡنِيَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضۡلِهِۦۗ وَٱلَّذِينَ يَبۡتَغُونَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ مِمَّا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُكُمۡ فَكَاتِبُوهُمۡ إِنۡ عَلِمۡتُمۡ فِيهِمۡ خَيۡرࣰ اۖ وَءَاتُوهُم مِّن مَّالِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِيٓ ءَاتَىٰكُمۡۚ وَلَا تُكۡرِهُواْ فَتَيَٰتِكُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡبِغَآءِ إِنۡ أَرَدۡنَ تَحَصُّنࣰ ا لِّتَبۡتَغُواْ عَرَضَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۚ وَمَن يُكۡرِههُّنَّ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ إِكۡرَٰهِهِنَّ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
24:33.en: And let those who cannot find a match keep chaste till Allah give them independence by His grace. And such of your slaves as seek a writing (of emancipation), write it for them if ye are aware of aught of good in them, and bestow upon them of the wealth of Allah which He hath bestowed upon you. Force not your slave-girls to whoredom that ye may seek enjoyment of the life of the world, if they would preserve their chastity. And if one force them, then (unto them), after their compulsion, lo! Allah will be Forgiving, Merciful

24:55.ar: وَعَدَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مِنكُمۡ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ لَيَسۡتَخۡلِفَنَّهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ كَمَا ٱسۡتَخۡلَفَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡ وَلَيُمَكِّنَنَّ لَهُمۡ دِينَهُمُ ٱلَّذِي ٱرۡتَضَىٰ لَهُمۡ وَلَيُبَدِّلَنَّهُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ خَوۡفِهِمۡ أَمۡنࣰ اۚ يَعۡبُدُونَنِي لَا يُشۡرِكُونَ بِي شَيۡـࣰٔ اۚ وَمَن كَفَرَ بَعۡدَ ذَٰلِكَ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡفَٰسِقُونَ
24:55.en: Allah hath promised such of you as believe and do good work that He will surely make them to succeed (the present rulers) in the earth even as He caused those who were before them to succeed (others); and that He will surely establish for them their religion which He hath approved for them, and will give them in exchange safety after their fear. They serve Me. They ascribe no thing as partner unto Me. Those who disbelieve henceforth, they are the miscreants

24:58.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لِيَسۡتَـٔۡذِنكُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُكُمۡ وَٱلَّذِينَ لَمۡ يَبۡلُغُواْ ٱلۡحُلُمَ مِنكُمۡ ثَلَٰثَ مَرَّٰتࣲۚ مِّن قَبۡلِ صَلَوٰةِ ٱلۡفَجۡرِ وَحِينَ تَضَعُونَ ثِيَابَكُم مِّنَ ٱلظَّهِيرَةِ وَمِنۢ بَعۡدِ صَلَوٰةِ ٱلۡعِشَآءِۚ ثَلَٰثُ عَوۡرَٰتࣲ لَّكُمۡۚ لَيۡسَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَلَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ جُنَاحُۢ بَعۡدَهُنَّۚ طَوَّٰفُونَ عَلَيۡكُم بَعۡضُكُمۡ عَلَىٰ بَعۡضࣲۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
24:58.en: O ye who believe! Let your slaves, and those of you who have not come to puberty, ask leave of you at three times (before they come into your presence): Before the prayer of dawn, and when ye lay aside your raiment for the heat of noon, and after the prayer of night. Three times of privacy for you. It is no sin for them or for you at other times, when some of you go round attendant upon others (if they come into your presence without leave). Thus Allah maketh clear the revelations for you. Allah is Knower, Wise

24:59.ar: وَإِذَا بَلَغَ ٱلۡأَطۡفَٰلُ مِنكُمُ ٱلۡحُلُمَ فَلۡيَسۡتَـٔۡذِنُواْ كَمَا ٱسۡتَـٔۡذَنَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
24:59.en: And when the children among you come to puberty then let them ask leave even as those before them used to ask it. Thus Allah maketh clear His revelations for you. Allah is Knower, Wise

24:62.ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ وَإِذَا كَانُواْ مَعَهُۥ عَلَىٰٓ أَمۡرࣲ جَامِعࣲ لَّمۡ يَذۡهَبُواْ حَتَّىٰ يَسۡتَـٔۡذِنُوهُۚ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَسۡتَـٔۡذِنُونَكَ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦۚ فَإِذَا ٱسۡتَـٔۡذَنُوكَ لِبَعۡضِ شَأۡنِهِمۡ فَأۡذَن لِّمَن شِئۡتَ مِنۡهُمۡ وَٱسۡتَغۡفِرۡ لَهُمُ ٱللَّهَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
24:62.en: They only are the true believers who believe in Allah and His messenger and, when they are with him on some common errand, go not away until they have asked leave of him. Lo! those who ask leave of thee, those are they who believe in Allah and His messenger. So, if they ask thy leave for some affair of theirs, give leave to whom thou wilt of them, and ask for them forgiveness of Allah. Lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

49:12.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱجۡتَنِبُواْ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلظَّنِّ إِنَّ بَعۡضَ ٱلظَّنِّ إِثۡمࣱۖ وَلَا تَجَسَّسُواْ وَلَا يَغۡتَب بَّعۡضُكُم بَعۡضًاۚ أَيُحِبُّ أَحَدُكُمۡ أَن يَأۡكُلَ لَحۡمَ أَخِيهِ مَيۡتࣰ ا فَكَرِهۡتُمُوهُۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ تَوَّابࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
49:12.en: O ye who believe! Shun much suspicion; for lo! some suspicion is a crime. And spy not, neither backbite one another. Would one of you love to eat the flesh of his dead brother? Ye abhor that (so abhor the other)! And keep your duty (to Allah). Lo! Allah is Relenting, Merciful

49:10.ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ إِخۡوَةࣱ فَأَصۡلِحُواْ بَيۡنَ أَخَوَيۡكُمۡۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُرۡحَمُونَ
49:10.en: The believers are naught else than brothers. Therefore make peace between your brethren and observe your duty to Allah that haply ye may obtain mercy

49:13.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّا خَلَقۡنَٰكُم مِّن ذَكَرࣲ وَأُنثَىٰ وَجَعَلۡنَٰكُمۡ شُعُوبࣰ ا وَقَبَآئِلَ لِتَعَارَفُوٓاْۚ إِنَّ أَكۡرَمَكُمۡ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ أَتۡقَىٰكُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرࣱ‏
49:13.en: O mankind! Lo! We have created you male and female, and have made you nations and tribes that ye may know one another. Lo! the noblest of you, in the sight of Allah, is the best in conduct. Lo! Allah is Knower, Aware

49:11.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا يَسۡخَرۡ قَوۡمࣱ مِّن قَوۡمٍ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَكُونُواْ خَيۡرࣰ ا مِّنۡهُمۡ وَلَا نِسَآءࣱ مِّن نِّسَآءٍ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَكُنَّ خَيۡرࣰ ا مِّنۡهُنَّۖ وَلَا تَلۡمِزُوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۡ وَلَا تَنَابَزُواْ بِٱلۡأَلۡقَٰبِۖ بِئۡسَ ٱلِٱسۡمُ ٱلۡفُسُوقُ بَعۡدَ ٱلۡإِيمَٰنِۚ وَمَن لَّمۡ يَتُبۡ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
49:11.en: O ye who believe! Let not a folk deride a folk who may be better than they (are), not let women (deride) women who may be better than they are; neither defame one another, nor insult one another by nicknames. Bad is the name of lewdness after faith. And whoso turneth not in repentance, such are evil-doers

4:11.ar: يُوصِيكُمُ ٱللَّهُ فِيٓ أَوۡلَٰدِكُمۡۖ لِلذَّكَرِ مِثۡلُ حَظِّ ٱلۡأُنثَيَيۡنِۚ فَإِن كُنَّ نِسَآءࣰ فَوۡقَ ٱثۡنَتَيۡنِ فَلَهُنَّ ثُلُثَا مَا تَرَكَۖ وَإِن كَانَتۡ وَٰحِدَةࣰ فَلَهَا ٱلنِّصۡفُۚ وَلِأَبَوَيۡهِ لِكُلِّ وَٰحِدࣲ مِّنۡهُمَا ٱلسُّدُسُ مِمَّا تَرَكَ إِن كَانَ لَهُۥ وَلَدࣱۚ فَإِن لَّمۡ يَكُن لَّهُۥ وَلَدࣱ وَوَرِثَهُۥٓ أَبَوَاهُ فَلِأُمِّهِ ٱلثُّلُثُۚ فَإِن كَانَ لَهُۥٓ إِخۡوَةࣱ فَلِأُمِّهِ ٱلسُّدُسُۚ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ وَصِيَّةࣲ يُوصِي بِهَآ أَوۡ دَيۡنٍۗ ءَابَآؤُكُمۡ وَأَبۡنَآؤُكُمۡ لَا تَدۡرُونَ أَيُّهُمۡ أَقۡرَبُ لَكُمۡ نَفۡعࣰ اۚ فَرِيضَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمࣰ ا
4:11.en: Allah chargeth you concerning (the provision for) your children: to the male the equivalent of the portion of two females, and if there be women more than two, then theirs is two-thirds of the inheritance, and if there be one (only) then the half. And to each of his parents a sixth of the inheritance, if he have a son; and if he have no son and his parents are his heirs, then to his mother appertaineth the third; and if he have brethren, then to his mother appertaineth the sixth, after any legacy he may have bequeathed, or debt (hath been paid). Your parents and your children: Ye know not which of them is nearer unto you in usefulness. It is an injunction from Allah. Lo! Allah is Knower, Wise

4:75.ar: وَمَا لَكُمۡ لَا تُقَٰتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡمُسۡتَضۡعَفِينَ مِنَ ٱلرِّجَالِ وَٱلنِّسَآءِ وَٱلۡوِلۡدَٰنِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَآ أَخۡرِجۡنَا مِنۡ هَٰذِهِ ٱلۡقَرۡيَةِ ٱلظَّالِمِ أَهۡلُهَا وَٱجۡعَل لَّنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ وَلِيࣰّ ا وَٱجۡعَل لَّنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ نَصِيرًا
4:75.en: How should ye not fight for the cause of Allah and of the feeble among men and of the women and the children who are crying: Our Lord! Bring us forth from out this town of which the people are oppressors! Oh, give us from thy presence some protecting friend! Oh, give us from Thy presence some defender

wzXw7BCVRs0.title: Seerah Halaqah: Social Rulings of Years Five and Six (Part 1)
wzXw7BCVRs0.one_line: Rulings revealed after the slander of Aishah in An-Nur and Al-Hujurat on gossip, privacy, modesty and respect, leading into the story of Banu Ubayriq.
wzXw7BCVRs0.summary: Continuing from the slander against Aishah, the sheikh draws out the lesson that a Muslim must refuse outright to take part in gossip, especially about someone's chastity, and walk away if it continues. He explains that Allah raised the early community by addressing real problems as they happened, and asks whether we will make the same decision today. He reviews the rulings of Surat An-Nur: seeking permission before entering homes, lowering the gaze for men and women, making marriage easy even for the poor, and children asking permission at three times of day. In the middle of these rules comes the promise of stewardship, safety and security for believers, which he says is reached through these everyday manners, beginning in the home. He moves to Surat Al-Hujurat: avoid bad assumptions about people, read words in the best light, reconcile quarrelling brothers, reject racism because only piety matters to Allah, and never mock or insult. He makes an exception for parents, whose job is to be watchful, and thanks his own strict father. He also covers inheritance rights for women and care for the weak, then introduces the story of a theft in Medina involving the sons of Ubayriq, Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man and his uncle.

outline.heading: Refuse to take part in gossip
outline.gist: When people speak about someone's chastity, the believer says it is not proper for us to speak of this.

outline.heading: Hard but essential; Allah teaches through real events
outline.gist: Walking away is difficult but central; the Quran raised the community by addressing problems as they occurred.

outline.heading: The choice before us today
outline.gist: Each of us must decide whether we will spread, entertain or refuse gossip.

outline.heading: Asking permission before entering homes
outline.gist: Respect privacy: do not enter or look into a house until permitted.

outline.heading: Lowering the gaze and making marriage easy
outline.gist: Both men and women are told to lower their gaze and guard chastity; society should help even poor people marry.

outline.heading: The promise of stewardship in An-Nur
outline.gist: A unique promise sits among the rules: believers will be granted authority, a firm religion and security.

outline.heading: Stewardship is earned through these rules
outline.gist: What Muslims hope for comes through adhering to these everyday commands.

outline.heading: Children asking permission at three times
outline.gist: Teaching children to knock at set times is where building a society begins.

outline.heading: Leaving a gathering with permission; respecting others
outline.gist: Believers do not walk out of a group without permission; be mindful and respectful of everyone around you.

outline.heading: Avoid bad assumptions
outline.gist: Suspicion does no good, fills the heart with bad feelings and harms brotherhood.

outline.heading: Parents are the exception
outline.gist: Parents are meant to be watchful; he thanks his strict father and warns that neglected children suffer.

outline.heading: Take words in the best way
outline.gist: If something can be read well or badly, read it well and move on; suspicion wastes time and energy.

outline.heading: Reconciliation and equality
outline.gist: Believers are brothers who must make peace between each other; colour, wealth and origin mean nothing to Allah.

outline.heading: Only piety matters
outline.gist: We all return to dust; what remains is goodness and purity of heart.

outline.heading: No mockery or name-calling
outline.gist: The one you mock may be better than you; respect governs entering, leaving and visiting.

outline.heading: Inheritance rights for women
outline.gist: Before these verses women inherited nothing and were even inherited; brothers today must not pressure sisters to give up their share.

outline.heading: Standing up for the weak
outline.gist: The Quran repeatedly demands care for those who cannot defend themselves.

outline.heading: Will we adopt these values?
outline.gist: Societies change when a generation holds to values the previous one neglected.

outline.heading: The theft story: the sons of Ubayriq and Qatadah's uncle
outline.gist: He introduces the players: troublesome brothers, the devout Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man, and his newly Muslim uncle.

35:3.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ ٱذۡكُرُواْ نِعۡمَتَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيۡكُمۡۚ هَلۡ مِنۡ خَٰلِقٍ غَيۡرُ ٱللَّهِ يَرۡزُقُكُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَۖ فَأَنَّىٰ تُؤۡفَكُونَ
35:3.en: O mankind! Remember Allah's grace toward you! Is there any creator other than Allah who provideth for you from the sky and the earth? There is no Allah save Him. Whither then are ye turned

35:4.ar: وَإِن يُكَذِّبُوكَ فَقَدۡ كُذِّبَتۡ رُسُلࣱ مِّن قَبۡلِكَۚ وَإِلَى ٱللَّهِ تُرۡجَعُ ٱلۡأُمُورُ
35:4.en: And if they deny thee, (O Muhammad), messengers (of Allah) were denied before thee. Unto Allah all things are brought back

35:5.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّ وَعۡدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقࣱّۖ فَلَا تَغُرَّنَّكُمُ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَلَا يَغُرَّنَّكُم بِٱللَّهِ ٱلۡغَرُورُ
35:5.en: O mankind! Lo! the promise of Allah is true. So let not the life of the world beguile you, and let not the (avowed) beguiler beguile you with regard to Allah

35:6.ar: إِنَّ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنَ لَكُمۡ عَدُوࣱّ فَٱتَّخِذُوهُ عَدُوًّاۚ إِنَّمَا يَدۡعُواْ حِزۡبَهُۥ لِيَكُونُواْ مِنۡ أَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
35:6.en: Lo! the devil is an enemy for you, so treat him as an enemy. He only summoneth his faction to be owners of the flaming Fire

35:7.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَهُمۡ عَذَابࣱ شَدِيدࣱۖ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ لَهُم مَّغۡفِرَةࣱ وَأَجۡرࣱ كَبِيرٌ
35:7.en: Those who disbelieve, theirs will be an awful doom; and those who believe and do good works, theirs will be forgiveness and a great reward

35:1.ar: ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ فَاطِرِ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ جَاعِلِ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ رُسُلًا أُوْلِيٓ أَجۡنِحَةࣲ مَّثۡنَىٰ وَثُلَٰثَ وَرُبَٰعَۚ يَزِيدُ فِي ٱلۡخَلۡقِ مَا يَشَآءُۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
35:1.en: Praise be to Allah, the Creator of the heavens and the earth, Who appointeth the angels messengers having wings two, three and four. He multiplieth in creation what He will. Lo! Allah is Able to do all things

35:2.ar: مَّا يَفۡتَحِ ٱللَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ مِن رَّحۡمَةࣲ فَلَا مُمۡسِكَ لَهَاۖ وَمَا يُمۡسِكۡ فَلَا مُرۡسِلَ لَهُۥ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
35:2.en: That which Allah openeth unto mankind of mercy none can withhold it; and that which He withholdeth none can release thereafter. He is the Mighty, the Wise

74:43.en: They will answer: We were not of those who prayed

74:44.en: Nor did we feed the wretched

74:45.en: We used to wade (in vain dispute) with (all) waders

74:46.en: And we used to deny the Day of Judgment

5:75.ar: مَّا ٱلۡمَسِيحُ ٱبۡنُ مَرۡيَمَ إِلَّا رَسُولࣱ قَدۡ خَلَتۡ مِن قَبۡلِهِ ٱلرُّسُلُ وَأُمُّهُۥ صِدِّيقَةࣱۖ كَانَا يَأۡكُلَانِ ٱلطَّعَامَۗ ٱنظُرۡ كَيۡفَ نُبَيِّنُ لَهُمُ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ ثُمَّ ٱنظُرۡ أَنَّىٰ يُؤۡفَكُونَ
5:75.en: The Messiah, son of Mary, was no other than a messenger, messengers (the like of whom) had passed away before him. And his mother was a saintly woman. And they both used to eat (earthly) food. See how We make the revelations clear for them, and see how they are turned away

34:13.ar: يَعۡمَلُونَ لَهُۥ مَا يَشَآءُ مِن مَّحَٰرِيبَ وَتَمَٰثِيلَ وَجِفَانࣲ كَٱلۡجَوَابِ وَقُدُورࣲ رَّاسِيَٰتٍۚ ٱعۡمَلُوٓاْ ءَالَ دَاوُۥدَ شُكۡرࣰ اۚ وَقَلِيلࣱ مِّنۡ عِبَادِيَ ٱلشَّكُورُ
34:13.en: They made for him what he willed: synagogues and statues, basins like wells and boilers built into the ground. Give thanks, O House of David! Few of My bondmen are thankful

24:11.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ جَآءُو بِٱلۡإِفۡكِ عُصۡبَةࣱ مِّنكُمۡۚ لَا تَحۡسَبُوهُ شَرࣰّ ا لَّكُمۖ بَلۡ هُوَ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡۚ لِكُلِّ ٱمۡرِيࣲٕ مِّنۡهُم مَّا ٱكۡتَسَبَ مِنَ ٱلۡإِثۡمِۚ وَٱلَّذِي تَوَلَّىٰ كِبۡرَهُۥ مِنۡهُمۡ لَهُۥ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمࣱ‏
24:11.en: Lo! they who spread the slander are a gang among you. Deem it not a bad thing for you; nay, it is good for you. Unto every man of them (will be paid) that which he hath earned of the sin; and as for him among them who had the greater share therein, his will be an awful doom

GbGRGurMVYM.speaker: adnan
GbGRGurMVYM.speaker_note: continues his Sunday English tafseer series at the London Muslim Mosque, recapping his previous session on Fatir
GbGRGurMVYM.title: Tafseer of Surah Fatir, Session 2 (35:3-7)
GbGRGurMVYM.one_line: The first two calls to all people in Fatir: remember Allah's blessings and be grateful, and do not let the low life or Shaytan deceive you.
GbGRGurMVYM.summary: He opens by warning against bending the Quran to an inherited agenda and argues that belief and practice are one package, so the Quran can list deeds before belief. After recapping Allah's credentials in the first two verses, he notes that the call to all people is the Makkan form of address, and that a God worth submitting to must be capable of everything, which is why simple signs expose false claimants to divinity. The first command is to remember Allah's blessing: no other creator provides for you, so why accept being lied to? Gratitude comes before happiness, and a hidden objection to one's lot makes submission impossible. These verses are statements for believers, not debating material, and he tells people to stop worrying about others' fate and trust Allah's justice. He links the ummah's identity to praise, through the names Muhammad and Ahmad and the Prophet's praise beneath the Throne, and explains gratitude for existence itself against the fear of nothingness. The second command: Allah's promise is true, so do not be deceived by the low life, which differs from the world itself, or by anyone misrepresenting Allah as only forgiving or only punishing. Shaytan is an enemy you must recognise. Gratitude and holding to the promise together make up personal submission.

outline.heading: Do not bend the Quran to your agenda
outline.gist: Companions warned against misusing the Quran; the first step for a student is to set aside the cultural agenda he inherited and let the verses shape how he thinks.

outline.heading: Submission across the cluster of surahs
outline.gist: Submitting means going with what Allah says whether you like it or not; the earlier surahs covered its hardest personal and communal forms, while Fatir asks who you submit to and why.

outline.heading: Why the Quran is not ordered logically: the mind needs a challenge
outline.gist: The Quran puts commands before belief and creed at the end, partly because the mind stays engaged when it has to assemble the pieces.

outline.heading: Belief and deeds are one package
outline.gist: Separating faith from action is foreign to the Quran; the people of hell list missed prayer and charity before denying the Day of Judgment because order does not matter in a single whole.

outline.heading: Question self-serving religious ideas
outline.gist: The idea that a few words save you regardless of conduct is convenient; politely question any religious concept that serves the person promoting it.

outline.heading: Recitation
outline.gist: He recites verses 3 and 4.

outline.heading: O mankind: the Makkan way of addressing people
outline.gist: Makkan surahs address all people; calls to the believers or the People of the Book mark a Madinan surah, because Makkah was about building the person, not issues of state and faith groups.

outline.heading: Accept no God less than capable of everything
outline.gist: Recapping Allah's resume, he says the Prophet's argument was that a lord lacking these attributes would not deserve submission; settling for half is selling yourself cheap.

outline.heading: Simple signs expose false gods
outline.gist: The Dajjal's physical defect and the Quran's point that Isa and his mother ate food show that the basis of faith is simple: one force controls everything.

outline.heading: Everyone else is as lost as you
outline.gist: Anyone posing as having it figured out without knowing where they came from and where they are going is just as lost; do not be fooled by suits and money.

outline.heading: He controls even a moment of ease
outline.gist: Even a passing feeling of peace in the heart is mercy that Allah sends or withholds.

outline.heading: First command: remember Allah's blessing
outline.gist: As Saba's communal submission began with gratitude, the personal form does too: is there any creator besides Allah who provides for you, with provision meaning everything you have?

outline.heading: Why do you accept being lied to?
outline.gist: Ifk is the worst kind of lie, the word used for the slander against Aisha; the verse asks why people let such lies steer them off the path.

outline.heading: Be grateful so you can be happy
outline.gist: You do not need happiness to be grateful; gratitude produces happiness, and hindsight often shows that hardships benefited you.

outline.heading: A hidden objection blocks submission
outline.gist: If deep down you object to the cards you or others were dealt, you cannot submit; this is why two surahs of the cluster open with praise.

outline.heading: These verses are not debate material
outline.gist: Unlike the argumentative passages of other surahs, this one states facts for the believer's own submission; using it to debate will backfire.

outline.heading: If they deny you, prophets before you were denied
outline.gist: Denial means refusing what seems most likely; the Prophet is consoled that all matters return to Allah, so do your part and let people be.

outline.heading: Stop worrying about where others will end up
outline.gist: Questions about remote tribes hide an objection to Allah's justice; be sure of your own destiny, do dawah if you can, and trust that no one will be wronged in His court.

outline.heading: An ummah named for praise
outline.gist: The ummah is called the people of praise; the Prophet is Muhammad and Ahmad, carries the banner of praise and will praise Allah beneath the Throne in a way that opens the judgment.

outline.heading: Gratitude for existence itself
outline.gist: The alternative to you was nothingness; no one truly wants to cease to exist, as the fear of death and of dreamless sleep shows, so simply being is the greatest blessing.

outline.heading: Life as a string of small highs
outline.gist: Atheist thinkers such as Richard Dawkins reduce life to moving from one small pleasure to the next, a sad conclusion for a great mind.

outline.heading: How the companions lived praise
outline.gist: The companions absorbed hamd for thirteen years; they asked each other how they were so the other would say alhamdulillah, a phrase new to the Arabs.

outline.heading: What is missing in the ummah
outline.gist: The basics are still present but spiritless, an empty vase; if they were alive we would think, act and feel differently.

outline.heading: Recitation of the second call
outline.gist: He recites verses 5 to 7 and flags the difference between gharur and ghurur.

outline.heading: Allah's promise is true
outline.gist: The promise is left open but means the whole deal: a mission, accountability on the Day of Judgment, and reward or punishment by what you do.

outline.heading: The world versus the low life
outline.gist: The world itself is not blameworthy, since prophets lived in it and the Hereafter is earned there; what is condemned is a life of low purpose, ethics and ambition that makes things seem worth more than they are.

outline.heading: Do not let the deceiver mislead you about Allah
outline.gist: The deceiver is left open: anyone who presents Allah falsely, whether as only forgiving so nothing matters, or as nothing but punishment, making you rigid and tense.

outline.heading: Take Shaytan as an enemy
outline.gist: Shaytan chose enmity toward Adam and his descendants; he has no power beyond whispering, but if you do not recognise him you will lose every confrontation.

outline.heading: The promise spelled out
outline.gist: Shaytan calls his party to the blaze; the next verse simply states severe punishment for deniers and forgiveness and great reward for believers who do good: this is the promise.

outline.heading: Two commands make up personal submission
outline.gist: Being grateful to the Creator and Provider, and holding to the promise without being distracted, are the two elements of submitting to Allah.

outline.heading: The slow build-up of Fatir
outline.gist: The surah rumbles through credentials and commands toward intense verses in the middle and keeps that pitch to the end; the companions felt such build-ups naturally.

outline.heading: Seeing the Quran in colour
outline.gist: Once you learn to listen to the Quran it turns from black and white to colour, and every reading, even his own tafsir of a surah, yields something new.

themes.label: Methodology: how to read texts, tafsir method, intellectual approach
themes.note: Set aside inherited agendas and let the verses dictate how you think.

themes.label: Eman: faith, certainty, doubt
themes.note: Belief and deeds cannot be separated; a faith of words alone is a self-serving idea.

themes.label: Tawhid and worship of Allah alone
themes.note: Only a God capable of everything deserves submission; simple signs expose false claimants.

themes.label: Gratitude (shukr) and appreciation
themes.note: The first command of personal submission is gratitude; it produces happiness, defines the ummah and starts with being grateful for existence.

themes.label: Justice and refusing oppression
themes.note: Trust that Allah wrongs no one instead of worrying about others' fate.

themes.label: Wealth, asceticism (zuhd), consumerism and money
themes.note: The world is not evil; the low life of possessions and low ambition is what deceives.

themes.label: Hope, fear and the balance between them
themes.note: Do not let anyone present Allah as only forgiving or only punishing.

themes.label: Shaytan: his methods and how to resist him
themes.note: Shaytan chose to be humanity's enemy; awareness of him is the defence.

Family of Dawud told to work in gratitude, the communal form of submission

hadith.gist: The Dajjal will perform feats people think only God can do but is one-eyed, a plain sign he is not God
The Prophet will carry the banner of praise and, prostrating beneath the Throne, be inspired with praises never offered before, which opens the judgment
The companions asked one another how they were so that the other would say alhamdulillah

maxims: Be grateful so you can be happy
Question any religious concept that serves the person preaching it

stories.who: The Dajjal at the end of time
stories.point: Even dazzling powers cannot make a flawed being God.

34:20.ar: وَلَقَدۡ صَدَّقَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ إِبۡلِيسُ ظَنَّهُۥ فَٱتَّبَعُوهُ إِلَّا فَرِيقࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
34:20.en: And Satan indeed found his calculation true concerning them, for they follow him, all save a group of true believers

34:21.ar: وَمَا كَانَ لَهُۥ عَلَيۡهِم مِّن سُلۡطَٰنٍ إِلَّا لِنَعۡلَمَ مَن يُؤۡمِنُ بِٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ مِمَّنۡ هُوَ مِنۡهَا فِي شَكࣲّۗ وَرَبُّكَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءٍ حَفِيظࣱ‏
34:21.en: And he had no warrant whatsoever against them, save that We would know him who believeth in the Hereafter from him who is in doubt thereof; and thy Lord (O Muhammad) taketh note of all things

34:24.ar: ۞قُلۡ مَن يَرۡزُقُكُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ قُلِ ٱللَّهُۖ وَإِنَّآ أَوۡ إِيَّاكُمۡ لَعَلَىٰ هُدًى أَوۡ فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
34:24.en: Say: Who giveth you provision from the sky and the earth? Say: Allah, Lo! we or you assuredly are rightly guided or in error manifest

34:25.ar: قُل لَّا تُسۡـَٔلُونَ عَمَّآ أَجۡرَمۡنَا وَلَا نُسۡـَٔلُ عَمَّا تَعۡمَلُونَ
34:25.en: Say: Ye will not be asked of what we committed, nor shall we be asked of what ye do

34:26.ar: قُلۡ يَجۡمَعُ بَيۡنَنَا رَبُّنَا ثُمَّ يَفۡتَحُ بَيۡنَنَا بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَهُوَ ٱلۡفَتَّاحُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ
34:26.en: Say: Our Lord will bring us all together, then He will judge between us with truth. He is the All-knowing Judge

34:27.ar: قُلۡ أَرُونِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَلۡحَقۡتُم بِهِۦ شُرَكَآءَۖ كَلَّاۚ بَلۡ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
34:27.en: Say: Show me those whom ye have joined unto Him as partners. Nay (ye dare not)! For He is Allah, the Mighty, the Wise

34:46.ar: ۞قُلۡ إِنَّمَآ أَعِظُكُم بِوَٰحِدَةٍۖ أَن تَقُومُواْ لِلَّهِ مَثۡنَىٰ وَفُرَٰدَىٰ ثُمَّ تَتَفَكَّرُواْۚ مَا بِصَاحِبِكُم مِّن جِنَّةٍۚ إِنۡ هُوَ إِلَّا نَذِيرࣱ لَّكُم بَيۡنَ يَدَيۡ عَذَابࣲ شَدِيدࣲ‏
34:46.en: Say (unto them, O Muhammad): I exhort you unto one thing only: that ye awake, for Allah's sake, by twos and singly, and then reflect: There is no madness in your comrade. He is naught else than a warner unto you in face of a terrific doom

34:47.ar: قُلۡ مَا سَأَلۡتُكُم مِّنۡ أَجۡرࣲ فَهُوَ لَكُمۡۖ إِنۡ أَجۡرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱللَّهِۖ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ شَهِيدࣱ‏
34:47.en: Say: Whatever reward I might have asked of you is yours. My reward is the affair of Allah only. He is Witness over all things

34:48.ar: قُلۡ إِنَّ رَبِّي يَقۡذِفُ بِٱلۡحَقِّ عَلَّٰمُ ٱلۡغُيُوبِ
34:48.en: Say: Lo! my Lord hurleth the truth. (He is) the Knower of Things Hidden

34:49.ar: قُلۡ جَآءَ ٱلۡحَقُّ وَمَا يُبۡدِئُ ٱلۡبَٰطِلُ وَمَا يُعِيدُ
34:49.en: Say: The Truth hath come, and falsehood showeth not its face and will not return

34:50.ar: قُلۡ إِن ضَلَلۡتُ فَإِنَّمَآ أَضِلُّ عَلَىٰ نَفۡسِيۖ وَإِنِ ٱهۡتَدَيۡتُ فَبِمَا يُوحِيٓ إِلَيَّ رَبِّيٓۚ إِنَّهُۥ سَمِيعࣱ قَرِيبࣱ‏
34:50.en: Say: If I err, I err only to my own loss, and if I am rightly guided it is because of that which my Lord hath revealed unto me. Lo! He is Hearer, Nigh

34:51.ar: وَلَوۡ تَرَىٰٓ إِذۡ فَزِعُواْ فَلَا فَوۡتَ وَأُخِذُواْ مِن مَّكَانࣲ قَرِيبࣲ‏
34:51.en: Couldst thou but see when they are terrified with no escape, and are seized from near at hand

34:52.ar: وَقَالُوٓاْ ءَامَنَّا بِهِۦ وَأَنَّىٰ لَهُمُ ٱلتَّنَاوُشُ مِن مَّكَانِۭ بَعِيدࣲ‏
34:52.en: And say: We (now) believe therein. But how can they reach (faith) from afar off

34:53.ar: وَقَدۡ كَفَرُواْ بِهِۦ مِن قَبۡلُۖ وَيَقۡذِفُونَ بِٱلۡغَيۡبِ مِن مَّكَانِۭ بَعِيدࣲ‏
34:53.en: When they disbelieved in it of yore. They aim at the unseen from afar off

34:54.ar: وَحِيلَ بَيۡنَهُمۡ وَبَيۡنَ مَا يَشۡتَهُونَ كَمَا فُعِلَ بِأَشۡيَاعِهِم مِّن قَبۡلُۚ إِنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ فِي شَكࣲّ مُّرِيبِۭ
34:54.en: And a gulf is set between them and that which they desire, as was done for people of their kind of old. Lo! they were in hopeless doubt

11:37.ar: وَٱصۡنَعِ ٱلۡفُلۡكَ بِأَعۡيُنِنَا وَوَحۡيِنَا وَلَا تُخَٰطِبۡنِي فِي ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوٓاْ إِنَّهُم مُّغۡرَقُونَ
11:37.en: Build the ship under Our eyes and by Our inspiration, and speak not unto Me on behalf of those who do wrong. Lo! they will be drowned

11:76.ar: يَٰٓإِبۡرَٰهِيمُ أَعۡرِضۡ عَنۡ هَٰذَآۖ إِنَّهُۥ قَدۡ جَآءَ أَمۡرُ رَبِّكَۖ وَإِنَّهُمۡ ءَاتِيهِمۡ عَذَابٌ غَيۡرُ مَرۡدُودࣲ‏
11:76.en: (It was said) O Abraham! Forsake this! Lo! thy Lord's commandment hath gone forth, and lo! there cometh unto them a doom which cannot be repelled

24:4.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يَرۡمُونَ ٱلۡمُحۡصَنَٰتِ ثُمَّ لَمۡ يَأۡتُواْ بِأَرۡبَعَةِ شُهَدَآءَ فَٱجۡلِدُوهُمۡ ثَمَٰنِينَ جَلۡدَةࣰ وَلَا تَقۡبَلُواْ لَهُمۡ شَهَٰدَةً أَبَدࣰ اۚ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡفَٰسِقُونَ
24:4.en: And those who accuse honourable women but bring not four witnesses, scourge them (with) eighty stripes and never (afterward) accept their testimony - They indeed are evil-doers

24:23.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَرۡمُونَ ٱلۡمُحۡصَنَٰتِ ٱلۡغَٰفِلَٰتِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِ لُعِنُواْ فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ وَلَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمࣱ‏
24:23.en: Lo! as for those who traduce virtuous, believing women (who are) careless, cursed are they in the world and the Hereafter. Theirs will be an awful doom

10:90.ar: ۞وَجَٰوَزۡنَا بِبَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱلۡبَحۡرَ فَأَتۡبَعَهُمۡ فِرۡعَوۡنُ وَجُنُودُهُۥ بَغۡيࣰ ا وَعَدۡوًاۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَآ أَدۡرَكَهُ ٱلۡغَرَقُ قَالَ ءَامَنتُ أَنَّهُۥ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِيٓ ءَامَنَتۡ بِهِۦ بَنُوٓاْ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ وَأَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ
10:90.en: And We brought the Children of Israel across the sea, and Pharaoh with his hosts pursued them in rebellion and transgression, till, when the (fate of) drowning overtook him, he exclaimed: I believe that there is no Allah save Him in Whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of those who surrender (unto Him)

dPK7aVr-Ezc.speaker: adnan
dPK7aVr-Ezc.speaker_note: final session of his Sunday Saba series; continues his own earlier sessions
dPK7aVr-Ezc.title: Tafseer of Surat Saba, Session 11: The Finale, Belief That Comes Too Late
dPK7aVr-Ezc.one_line: Recap of the five narratives of 34:46-50, then the surah's finale 34:51-54: the terror of resurrection, belief that comes too late, and the danger of doubt.
dPK7aVr-Ezc.summary: He first explains that clusters of verses beginning with the command to say serve as dialogue, debate or narrative, and reviews the five narratives of verses 46 to 50. Reflection does not mean switching off the mind: as with trust in the scientific method, deep thought leads to conviction that Allah's commands are right even when their effects are not yet visible, so faith should rest on observing the universe, life, history and oneself, not on numerical curiosities. He adds that modern people should not condemn past generations arrogantly, since every age has blind spots, as ours will be judged for driving cars. The finale then pictures the resurrection: people wake startled, knowing nothing can be changed, because the door of repentance that was open all their lives is now shut. They cry that they believe, but faith is acceptance of the unseen; once seen, it cannot be obtained easily from so far away, after a life spent rejecting it. Explaining a word in verse 53 used for slandering women, he digresses on the conditions for that punishment and argues that laws only protect values a society already holds, so mentalities must change first. The surah ends with a barrier between them and what they desire because they lived in doubt, so he urges listeners to resolve their doubts now through reflection.

outline.heading: Three uses of the repeated command to say
outline.gist: A run of verses beginning with 'say' teaches either dialogue, debate points or a general narrative.

outline.heading: Two clusters in Saba
outline.gist: The first cluster was dialogue with opponents; the second is the community's narrative.

outline.heading: First narrative: stop and think
outline.gist: Reflection ensures you make conscious choices you can defend at the accounting.

outline.heading: Submission is not switching off the brain
outline.gist: Deep thought leads to trust in Allah's word, as scientists trust a method before seeing results.

outline.heading: Build faith on constants, not curiosities
outline.gist: Faith built on number patterns or one answered prayer collapses; build it on the universe, life, history and your own story.

outline.heading: Your companion is not mad
outline.gist: Honest reflection concludes the Prophet was a truthful warner.

outline.heading: Second narrative: a culture of service
outline.gist: Muslims succeeded when they served; running masjids like businesses betrays this.

outline.heading: Third narrative: truth backed by knowledge of the unseen
outline.gist: Allah's rulings are right because He knows what we cannot foresee.

outline.heading: Do not condemn past generations
outline.gist: Judging the past arrogantly, even on slavery or women's treatment, blinds us to our own era's mistakes.

outline.heading: Every era has blind spots
outline.gist: Future generations may condemn us for cars; only rare innovators see beyond their time, while Allah knows the unseen.

outline.heading: Fourth narrative: truth is the constant
outline.gist: Falsehood cannot start or sustain anything; measure everything against the truth.

outline.heading: Fifth narrative: humility
outline.gist: Mistakes are mine to fix; good is Allah's guidance, so let Him celebrate your successes.

outline.heading: Recitation of the finale
outline.gist: He begins reciting the last verses.

outline.heading: Waking startled at the resurrection
outline.gist: Faza' is panic on suddenly becoming aware; no one wakes peacefully from the grave.

outline.heading: Nothing can be changed anymore
outline.gist: Every morning in this life was a chance to turn around; on that day the books are closed.

outline.heading: The door of repentance open before you were born
outline.gist: Allah created the door of repentance before creating people, and it stays open until the sun rises from the west.

outline.heading: Unrepented sins become permanent
outline.gist: Forgiveness after resurrection is costly; people will beg for others' good deeds, and no one escapes being brought.

outline.heading: Makan: three meanings in three verses
outline.gist: Only the first use of 'place' is literal: they are taken from a place close to the judgment.

outline.heading: The last snapshot of the Day of Judgment
outline.gist: The surah has shown several scenes of that Day; this one ties the surah together.

outline.heading: We believe in it now
outline.gist: Seeing the truth, everyone declares belief.

outline.heading: Faith means accepting the unseen
outline.gist: Once seen, belief is no longer iman; only Allah's essence remains unseen even in Paradise.

outline.heading: The hundred mercies
outline.gist: One mercy is shared by all creatures in this world; the ninety-nine are spread on the Day of Judgment, so that even Iblis hopes.

outline.heading: Tanawush: obtaining it easily
outline.gist: The rare word means getting something without effort; belief cannot be picked up easily at that point.

outline.heading: From a faraway place
outline.gist: The distance is in their story, not space; believers spent their lives holding on to the words they now say lightly.

outline.heading: When Allah ends the discussion
outline.gist: Nuh and Ibrahim were told not to plead for those already judged.

outline.heading: They disbelieved it before
outline.gist: They spent their lives rejecting the very statement they now make.

outline.heading: Qadhf: casting, and slandering a woman's honour
outline.gist: The word is used for throwing and for impugning a woman's chastity, one of the few socially punishable sins.

outline.heading: The punishment and its conditions
outline.gist: An accuser without four upright eyewitnesses of the act itself is lashed eighty times.

outline.heading: Umar demanding four witnesses
outline.gist: A companion who reported seeing adultery was warned by Umar to bring witnesses or be lashed.

outline.heading: Public versus private sin
outline.gist: Only flagrant public acts are socially punishable; private sin is equally forbidden but left to the hereafter, and spying is itself punished.

outline.heading: Laws protect values a society already holds
outline.gist: Strict punishments imposed where people do not see a sin as wrong cause chaos; change mentalities first.

outline.heading: Drugs, tobacco and marijuana
outline.gist: Harsh drug laws failed while campaigns that changed attitudes cut smoking; marijuana is now portrayed as a cure-all.

outline.heading: The shamelessness the law targets
outline.gist: Islam does not pry into homes; the punishment targets those who flaunt sin before the public, and it was rarely applied.

outline.heading: Casting conclusions at the unseen
outline.gist: Allah casts the truth because He knows; they cast guesses about the unseen with no evidence.

outline.heading: Recitation of the last verse
outline.gist: He recites the closing verse.

outline.heading: A barrier between them and what they desire
outline.gist: They want their declaration of faith accepted as they watch others go to Paradise, but a barrier is set.

outline.heading: Their kind before them
outline.gist: Shiya originally means those of the same kind or family, a word later narrowed to a sectarian sense.

outline.heading: Ninety-nine percent belief is doubt
outline.gist: Iblis was given power only to separate those who believe in the hereafter from those in doubt; certainty must be complete.

outline.heading: A question on Firawn's late belief
outline.gist: The same rule applied to earlier people, such as Firawn's belief at drowning.

outline.heading: Resolve your doubt now
outline.gist: He summarizes the finale and sends listeners back to the one advice: reflect until you can live without doubt.

35:3.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ ٱذۡكُرُواْ نِعۡمَتَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيۡكُمۡۚ هَلۡ مِنۡ خَٰلِقٍ غَيۡرُ ٱللَّهِ يَرۡزُقُكُم مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَۖ فَأَنَّىٰ تُؤۡفَكُونَ
35:3.en: O mankind! Remember Allah's grace toward you! Is there any creator other than Allah who provideth for you from the sky and the earth? There is no Allah save Him. Whither then are ye turned

35:5.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّ وَعۡدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقࣱّۖ فَلَا تَغُرَّنَّكُمُ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَلَا يَغُرَّنَّكُم بِٱللَّهِ ٱلۡغَرُورُ
35:5.en: O mankind! Lo! the promise of Allah is true. So let not the life of the world beguile you, and let not the (avowed) beguiler beguile you with regard to Allah

35:6.ar: إِنَّ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنَ لَكُمۡ عَدُوࣱّ فَٱتَّخِذُوهُ عَدُوًّاۚ إِنَّمَا يَدۡعُواْ حِزۡبَهُۥ لِيَكُونُواْ مِنۡ أَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلسَّعِيرِ
35:6.en: Lo! the devil is an enemy for you, so treat him as an enemy. He only summoneth his faction to be owners of the flaming Fire

35:7.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَهُمۡ عَذَابࣱ شَدِيدࣱۖ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ لَهُم مَّغۡفِرَةࣱ وَأَجۡرࣱ كَبِيرٌ
35:7.en: Those who disbelieve, theirs will be an awful doom; and those who believe and do good works, theirs will be forgiveness and a great reward

35:8.ar: أَفَمَن زُيِّنَ لَهُۥ سُوٓءُ عَمَلِهِۦ فَرَءَاهُ حَسَنࣰ اۖ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُضِلُّ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهۡدِي مَن يَشَآءُۖ فَلَا تَذۡهَبۡ نَفۡسُكَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ حَسَرَٰتٍۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمُۢ بِمَا يَصۡنَعُونَ
35:8.en: Is he, the evil of whose deeds is made fairseeming unto him so that he deemeth it good, (other than Satan's dupe)? Allah verily sendeth whom He will astray, and guideth whom He will; so let not thy soul expire in sighings for them. Lo! Allah is Aware of what they do

35:9.ar: وَٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَرۡسَلَ ٱلرِّيَٰحَ فَتُثِيرُ سَحَابࣰ ا فَسُقۡنَٰهُ إِلَىٰ بَلَدࣲ مَّيِّتࣲ فَأَحۡيَيۡنَا بِهِ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ بَعۡدَ مَوۡتِهَاۚ كَذَٰلِكَ ٱلنُّشُورُ
35:9.en: And Allah it is Who sendeth the winds and they raise a cloud; then We lead it unto a dead land and revive therewith the earth after its death. Such is the Resurrection

35:1.ar: ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ فَاطِرِ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ جَاعِلِ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ رُسُلًا أُوْلِيٓ أَجۡنِحَةࣲ مَّثۡنَىٰ وَثُلَٰثَ وَرُبَٰعَۚ يَزِيدُ فِي ٱلۡخَلۡقِ مَا يَشَآءُۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
35:1.en: Praise be to Allah, the Creator of the heavens and the earth, Who appointeth the angels messengers having wings two, three and four. He multiplieth in creation what He will. Lo! Allah is Able to do all things

35:2.ar: مَّا يَفۡتَحِ ٱللَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ مِن رَّحۡمَةࣲ فَلَا مُمۡسِكَ لَهَاۖ وَمَا يُمۡسِكۡ فَلَا مُرۡسِلَ لَهُۥ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
35:2.en: That which Allah openeth unto mankind of mercy none can withhold it; and that which He withholdeth none can release thereafter. He is the Mighty, the Wise

35:4.ar: وَإِن يُكَذِّبُوكَ فَقَدۡ كُذِّبَتۡ رُسُلࣱ مِّن قَبۡلِكَۚ وَإِلَى ٱللَّهِ تُرۡجَعُ ٱلۡأُمُورُ
35:4.en: And if they deny thee, (O Muhammad), messengers (of Allah) were denied before thee. Unto Allah all things are brought back

9:29.ar: قَٰتِلُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَلَا بِٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِ وَلَا يُحَرِّمُونَ مَا حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَلَا يَدِينُونَ دِينَ ٱلۡحَقِّ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ حَتَّىٰ يُعۡطُواْ ٱلۡجِزۡيَةَ عَن يَدࣲ وَهُمۡ صَٰغِرُونَ
9:29.en: Fight against such of those who have been given the Scripture as believe not in Allah nor the Last Day, and forbid not that which Allah hath forbidden by His messenger, and follow not the Religion of Truth, until they pay the tribute readily, being brought low

2:256.ar: لَآ إِكۡرَاهَ فِي ٱلدِّينِۖ قَد تَّبَيَّنَ ٱلرُّشۡدُ مِنَ ٱلۡغَيِّۚ فَمَن يَكۡفُرۡ بِٱلطَّٰغُوتِ وَيُؤۡمِنۢ بِٱللَّهِ فَقَدِ ٱسۡتَمۡسَكَ بِٱلۡعُرۡوَةِ ٱلۡوُثۡقَىٰ لَا ٱنفِصَامَ لَهَاۗ وَٱللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ
2:256.en: There is no compulsion in religion. The right direction is henceforth distinct from error. And he who rejecteth false deities and believeth in Allah hath grasped a firm handhold which will never break. Allah is Hearer, Knower

2:281.ar: وَٱتَّقُواْ يَوۡمࣰ ا تُرۡجَعُونَ فِيهِ إِلَى ٱللَّهِۖ ثُمَّ تُوَفَّىٰ كُلُّ نَفۡسࣲ مَّا كَسَبَتۡ وَهُمۡ لَا يُظۡلَمُونَ
2:281.en: And guard yourselves against a day in which ye will be brought back to Allah. Then every soul will be paid in full that which it hath earned, and they will not be wronged

24:30.ar: قُل لِّلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ يَغُضُّواْ مِنۡ أَبۡصَٰرِهِمۡ وَيَحۡفَظُواْ فُرُوجَهُمۡۚ ذَٰلِكَ أَزۡكَىٰ لَهُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ خَبِيرُۢ بِمَا يَصۡنَعُونَ
24:30.en: Tell the believing men to lower their gaze and be modest. That is purer for them. Lo! Allah is aware of what they do

73Ya6c8TS5M.speaker_note: continues his Sunday English tafseer of Fatir, recapping his own earlier sessions and stating his personal position on abrogation
73Ya6c8TS5M.title: Tafseer of Surah Fatir, Session 3 (35:7-9)
73Ya6c8TS5M.one_line: Gratitude plus not being deceived as the prerequisites of submission, each surah's self-evident premises, abrogation, and the person whose evil looks good to him.
73Ya6c8TS5M.summary: He recaps the two opening commands and argues that together they are the precondition for submission: gratitude is a whole outlook on existence, which a competitive society erodes into anxiety, and not being deceived means knowing the picture continues after death. Some people have one without the other, and he doubts most Muslims hold both. Verse 7 seems obvious, but each long surah lays down its own self-evident premises before drawing conclusions, so reading a verse through another surah's premises causes confusion. This leads to abrogation: he rejects the claim that recited verses cancel others, such as using a verse from al-Tawbah to erase the verse of no compulsion, notes that revelation order is mostly uncertain, and holds that anything abrogated was removed during the Prophet's lifetime. Those who argue otherwise usually carry an agenda. Verse 8 describes a person whose bad deeds are made to look good; using the saying on four kinds of knowers, he warns that the one ignorant of his own ignorance cannot be helped, and that becoming so takes years of blaming others. Do not destroy yourself grieving over such people. Verse 9 shows resurrection as simply as rain reviving dead land.

outline.heading: Fatir: an almost storyless surah
outline.gist: Unlike the first two surahs of the cluster, Fatir treats submission methodically, with almost no stories, which is rare for a surah of its length.

outline.heading: Recap of the credentials and two commands
outline.gist: He reviews Allah's attributes in the opening verses and the two calls: remember His blessing, and do not be deceived by the low life.

outline.heading: Gratitude is an outlook, not a phrase
outline.gist: Either you feel privileged simply to exist or you keep a long list of standards before you can feel happy; there is no middle way.

outline.heading: Competition breeds anxiety without gratitude
outline.gist: In a competitive social, financial and educational system the gap with those ahead causes depression and worthlessness unless you see existence itself as a gift.

outline.heading: Gratitude plus not being deceived enables submission
outline.gist: Be grateful for what you have however little, and know there is a meticulous judgment coming, so possessions and status cannot fool you; without both you cannot submit.

outline.heading: Grateful but deceived, or undeceived but ungrateful
outline.gist: Some non-believers are content yet think this life is everything; others see through the world but are bitter toward existence. Neither is ready to submit.

outline.heading: How many Muslims hold both?
outline.gist: Saying alhamdulillah is not inner gratitude; he doubts most Muslims truly have both concepts clearly grasped.

outline.heading: Why state the obvious: each surah's premises
outline.gist: The verse on punishment and reward looks self-evident, but each long surah states the maxims it needs, like the initial equations in a physics problem, so it is not repetition.

outline.heading: Do not force one surah's verse onto another
outline.gist: Reading a verse through premises another surah deliberately left out produces a salad, as with the fighting passages of al-Tawbah read without its own opening maxims.

outline.heading: Abrogation within the Quran
outline.gist: Cross-matching blindly gave rise to claims of naskh; the Quran superseding earlier scriptures is accepted, but claims that recited verses cancel others are another matter.

outline.heading: One verse used to erase a hundred
outline.gist: Some claimed the fighting verse of al-Tawbah cancelled well over a hundred passages, including no compulsion in religion and the verses on freedom of choice.

outline.heading: Self-evident statements prevent magical thinking
outline.gist: Each surah's opening concepts are needed for its conclusions; strange readings usually come from not knowing how to navigate a surah.

outline.heading: How surahs were assembled
outline.gist: Answering a question, he explains that the Prophet told the companions where to place verses, and that some surahs are tied to context while general ones like Fatir carry no stories.

outline.heading: Revelation order is mostly uncertain
outline.gist: Only that Makkan came before Madinan is certain; relative order is probabilistic, so timing is a weak basis for abrogation.

outline.heading: His position: what was abrogated left the Quran
outline.gist: He holds that whatever was abrogated was removed in wording and ruling during the Prophet's life; declaring a recited word of God void is beyond what he would ever dare.

outline.heading: Abrogation and agendas
outline.gist: In his experience those who push abrogation want violence or a political goal; every verse has a place to be practised and apparent contradictions come from not knowing the surah.

outline.heading: Learning to navigate the Quran
outline.gist: Seeing each surah as a unit with a connecting theme already puts you ahead; the early generations sensed this naturally because they knew the language deeply.

outline.heading: Fatir's five premises and its anchor verse
outline.gist: Gratitude, the Day of Judgment, not being deceived, Shaytan as enemy and the consequences of deeds are the premises the surah builds on toward an anchor verse and a climax near the end.

outline.heading: Recitation
outline.gist: He recites verse 8.

outline.heading: The one whose evil deeds are made to look good
outline.gist: These verses bring home the warning against being deceived: how can anyone help a person doing wrong who is convinced he is doing right?

outline.heading: Four kinds of knowers
outline.gist: One who knows and knows it, one who knows but has forgotten, one who does not know and knows it, and one ignorant of his own ignorance, who must be left to life's hard lessons.

outline.heading: No self-insight: always someone else's fault
outline.gist: The professor hates me, the boss is racist: such a person never sees his shortcomings. Your job is to self-regulate, question yourself and revise your approach all the time.

outline.heading: The unstated end of the sentence
outline.gist: The verse leaves out that nothing can be done for him; Allah misguides and guides whom He wills, or those who will it, and both readings are valid.

outline.heading: Do not destroy yourself with grief over them
outline.gist: Sorrow and regret over those who feel no guilt waste you; focus on people with some insight whom you can actually help.

outline.heading: Yasna'un: deeds of complex making
outline.gist: Amal is a deed, fi'l a repeated act, sa'y a long-term aim, and sun' a complex, premeditated practice, the same word used for lowering the gaze.

outline.heading: How one becomes ignorant of one's ignorance
outline.gist: No child or young adult is like this; it takes years of stopping self-criticism, blaming others and silencing the conscience, and such a person cannot submit.

outline.heading: Recitation
outline.gist: He recites verse 9 and asks why it is placed here.

outline.heading: Resurrection as simple as rain on dead land
outline.gist: Verse 9 comments on the promise of verse 5: winds drive clouds to dead land and it lives again, and resurrection is that simple and happens around you constantly.

outline.heading: Why the companions needed no such breakdown
outline.gist: A companion would find this explanation obvious and want only the practical behaviour; we have lost the conceptual grasp, so it must be rebuilt first.

34:46.ar: ۞قُلۡ إِنَّمَآ أَعِظُكُم بِوَٰحِدَةٍۖ أَن تَقُومُواْ لِلَّهِ مَثۡنَىٰ وَفُرَٰدَىٰ ثُمَّ تَتَفَكَّرُواْۚ مَا بِصَاحِبِكُم مِّن جِنَّةٍۚ إِنۡ هُوَ إِلَّا نَذِيرࣱ لَّكُم بَيۡنَ يَدَيۡ عَذَابࣲ شَدِيدࣲ‏
34:46.en: Say (unto them, O Muhammad): I exhort you unto one thing only: that ye awake, for Allah's sake, by twos and singly, and then reflect: There is no madness in your comrade. He is naught else than a warner unto you in face of a terrific doom

34:47.ar: قُلۡ مَا سَأَلۡتُكُم مِّنۡ أَجۡرࣲ فَهُوَ لَكُمۡۖ إِنۡ أَجۡرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱللَّهِۖ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ شَهِيدࣱ‏
34:47.en: Say: Whatever reward I might have asked of you is yours. My reward is the affair of Allah only. He is Witness over all things

34:48.ar: قُلۡ إِنَّ رَبِّي يَقۡذِفُ بِٱلۡحَقِّ عَلَّٰمُ ٱلۡغُيُوبِ
34:48.en: Say: Lo! my Lord hurleth the truth. (He is) the Knower of Things Hidden

34:49.ar: قُلۡ جَآءَ ٱلۡحَقُّ وَمَا يُبۡدِئُ ٱلۡبَٰطِلُ وَمَا يُعِيدُ
34:49.en: Say: The Truth hath come, and falsehood showeth not its face and will not return

34:50.ar: قُلۡ إِن ضَلَلۡتُ فَإِنَّمَآ أَضِلُّ عَلَىٰ نَفۡسِيۖ وَإِنِ ٱهۡتَدَيۡتُ فَبِمَا يُوحِيٓ إِلَيَّ رَبِّيٓۚ إِنَّهُۥ سَمِيعࣱ قَرِيبࣱ‏
34:50.en: Say: If I err, I err only to my own loss, and if I am rightly guided it is because of that which my Lord hath revealed unto me. Lo! He is Hearer, Nigh

4:34.ar: ٱلرِّجَالُ قَوَّٰمُونَ عَلَى ٱلنِّسَآءِ بِمَا فَضَّلَ ٱللَّهُ بَعۡضَهُمۡ عَلَىٰ بَعۡضࣲ وَبِمَآ أَنفَقُواْ مِنۡ أَمۡوَٰلِهِمۡۚ فَٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتُ قَٰنِتَٰتٌ حَٰفِظَٰتࣱ لِّلۡغَيۡبِ بِمَا حَفِظَ ٱللَّهُۚ وَٱلَّٰتِي تَخَافُونَ نُشُوزَهُنَّ فَعِظُوهُنَّ وَٱهۡجُرُوهُنَّ فِي ٱلۡمَضَاجِعِ وَٱضۡرِبُوهُنَّۖ فَإِنۡ أَطَعۡنَكُمۡ فَلَا تَبۡغُواْ عَلَيۡهِنَّ سَبِيلًاۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيࣰّ ا كَبِيرࣰ ا
4:34.en: Men are in charge of women, because Allah hath made the one of them to excel the other, and because they spend of their property (for the support of women). So good women are the obedient, guarding in secret that which Allah hath guarded. As for those from whom ye fear rebellion, admonish them and banish them to beds apart, and scourge them. Then if they obey you, seek not a way against them. Lo! Allah is ever High, Exalted, Great

EevbkcPjbNk.title: Tafseer of Surat Saba, Session 10: The Five Narratives Muslims Carry
EevbkcPjbNk.one_line: Saba 34:46-50 as five narratives Muslims carry to the world: think for yourself, serve without asking, know Allah, hold to truth, and stay humble.
EevbkcPjbNk.summary: He reads the five verses that each begin with the command to say, and presents them as the narrative Muslims carry to everyone. First, our only advice to all people is to stop and think for Allah's sake, alone or with others: most of life is routine inherited from culture and consumerism, many people never ask where they are heading, and each person must make their choices their own because they will answer for them alone. He describes having to make that decision himself as a teenager, and says one convinced person is worth thousands of the undecided, as in the four men sent to Amr ibn al-As each counted as a thousand. Second, we ask nothing in return; our reward is from Allah, which makes institutions run like businesses hard to reconcile with the Quran. Third, our idea of God: He casts only truth, so everything He commands is in our interest, and He knows the unseen, which is true power. Fourth, truth is the only constant; falsehood can neither begin nor repeat anything, so truth must outweigh everything on the scale of each decision, from waking for Fajr to how we treat family. Fifth, humility: our mistakes are our own, and any guidance we find is Allah's gift.

outline.heading: Recitation of verse 46
outline.gist: He recites the verse beginning a run of commands to say.

outline.heading: One piece of advice for everyone
outline.gist: This is a narrative, not a dialogue: stand for Allah's sake, in pairs or alone.

outline.heading: Tafakkur: deep, deliberate thought
outline.gist: The Quran repeatedly commands thinking that draws parallels and conclusions about Allah and what we should do.

outline.heading: A tender form of advice
outline.gist: The word chosen for advice is gentle, like the tone used with a spouse.

outline.heading: Routines we never chose
outline.gist: School, marriage, a house and morning coffee come from the culture we are born into, not objective choices.

outline.heading: Sucked into the current of consumerism
outline.gist: Many people simply keep going through life's waves without asking where they are heading.

outline.heading: Never asking the question
outline.gist: Some reach their nineties uninterested in the question, and will be unprepared for accountability.

outline.heading: Making his faith his own as a teenager
outline.gist: At about sixteen he had to decide whether Islam was his choice or his father's, and came out with conviction.

outline.heading: Turn your brain on
outline.gist: Islam does not ask people to switch off their minds; it commands thought so each can carry his own consequences.

outline.heading: One convinced person is worth thousands
outline.gist: Those stuck in the middle are of little use; Umar sent four men to Amr ibn al-As, each counted as a thousand.

outline.heading: Hoping a word reaches the next Salahuddin
outline.gist: You never know whose life your encouragement will change.

outline.heading: Your companion is not mad, only a warner
outline.gist: Honest reflection leads to the conclusion that the Prophet only warned of a severe day.

outline.heading: Second narrative: we ask nothing from you
outline.gist: Our reward is from Allah, who witnesses everything; serving people is not a transaction.

outline.heading: Institutions run like businesses
outline.gist: He has long feared this verse; the constant asking of Islamic institutions is hard to reconcile with it.

outline.heading: Win hearts and the money follows
outline.gist: The Prophet wanted conviction, not money, and convinced people funded what was needed.

outline.heading: Third narrative: the word order of verse 48
outline.gist: The description of the Lord is moved to the end of the verse for emphasis.

outline.heading: Why theology comes third in a social surah
outline.gist: In social contexts how we treat others comes first; He casts only the truth.

outline.heading: He commands only what is in your interest
outline.gist: Since He projects only truth, every command and prohibition is for our benefit.

outline.heading: Knowledge is real power
outline.gist: Our only weakness is not knowing what comes next, as in the scene from The Matrix.

outline.heading: The Knower of the unseen has no weakness
outline.gist: Allah has no ignorance and so is the most powerful; our knowledge is a drop in an ocean.

outline.heading: Fourth narrative: the truth has come
outline.gist: The truth is here and permanent.

outline.heading: Falsehood neither begins nor repeats
outline.gist: An old Arabic expression: falsehood has no power to start anything or sustain itself.

outline.heading: Truth on the scale of every decision
outline.gist: Life is a series of decisions weighed on a scale; where truth is involved it must outweigh everything.

outline.heading: Waking for Fajr
outline.gist: If truth is the constant, tiredness and cold never outweigh the prayer.

outline.heading: Living by truth in every relationship
outline.gist: Truth is clear in the book; stand with it against oppression and in dealings with spouse, children and community.

outline.heading: Fifth narrative: my errors are my own
outline.gist: If I go astray it is my own doing and harm; if I am guided it is through what Allah reveals.

outline.heading: A narrative of humility, not balance
outline.gist: The good we do is His generosity; the mistakes are ours to fix and carry.

outline.heading: All-Hearing and Near
outline.gist: The names chosen carry closeness; He is nearer than the jugular vein.

outline.heading: No credit for following guidance
outline.gist: Claiming credit for following His guidance is vanity.

outline.heading: Recap: think for yourself and serve
outline.gist: Do not follow routine or people blindly; Muslims are here to serve, not to take.

outline.heading: Serve, do not try to control
outline.gist: Trying to control everything is playing Allah's role; serve well, then leave the rest, and hold to the narratives of God, truth and humility.
